content:
anya: Heads-up — running long-context fuzzing (24k tokens) on H100 pools and seeing KV cache resident memory keep growing even after eviction should have reclaimed pages. Attaching quick logs below and a short repro command.

ryan: thanks. does this happen on A100 too or only H100? any differences with multi-stream concurrency?

anya: repro was on h100-prod-1 and h100-canary. A100s look better (growth ~stable). H100 shows ~0.8GB/min growth during a 5k->24k ramp. command: `./tools/kv_fuzz --model=gptx-16k --tokens=24000 --batch=1 --vram-budget=24G`

felix: paste of the eviction log fragment I pulled from the run:
```
[2025-11-09T14:22:05Z] KVPageTable::evict_range(0x7f3a...): requested 64 pages
[2025-11-09T14:22:05Z] evicted 63 pages, freed 63 * 2MB
[2025-11-09T14:22:05Z] page_table.stats: entries=102348, free_slots=12, dirty_fragments=7
[2025-11-09T14:22:06Z] eviction missed 1 page: index 102349 (already mapped?)
[2025-11-09T14:22:06Z] pool_resident=21.4GB
```
anya: note "eviction missed 1 page: index 102349 (already mapped?)" — we see this message repeatedly and pool_resident doesn't drop fully.

ryan: interesting. could be double-free/dup-count or a race where eviction removes mapping but some stream re-inserts a stale ref. Any nvprof/tracing?

anya: attached a small timeline from our perf trace:
```
T0 allocate page 102349 -> map
T1 token decode hits, append KV -> mark hot
T2 eviction scan picks page 102349 -> unmap
T3 decoding CUDA kernel still referencing older KV ptr -> rebind path does `insert_or_inc(102349)`
T4 page_table reports entry_count++ but the physical page was never actually freed due to ref mismatch
```

irene: on RTX6000 we saw similar but different symptoms: fragmentation (lots of 1-page holes) rather than monotonic growth. suspect allocator granularity + PCIe ordering differences. H100's multi-engine concurrent compute/ccopy ordering might allow remap races.

felix: repro across GPUs: H100: leak 0.6-1.0GB/min; A100: pretty stable (<50MB drift over same run); RTX6000: fragmentation and slower OOM due to holes.

ryan: hypothesizing root cause: our page-table insert path isn't atomic with eviction when there are concurrent kernels across streams. On H100 the reorder window is larger so stale kernel can touch freed slot and we end up incrementing live_count without actually increasing refs to the freed block (refcount mismatch). Also our free-list merge/compaction assumes single-threaded eviction.

anya: quick proposed fix: make insert_or_inc use an epoch-based check: each eviction increments global_epoch; when unmapping we bump epoch on slot, and insert checks that slot_epoch == current_epoch before using. If mismatched, allocate fresh slot. Also add an atomic CAS to update slot state in hot path to avoid ABA.

felix: patch prototype done: `kv_pt::try_acquire(slot, epoch)` uses atomic CAS on a 64-bit word (state|epoch). Ran microbench on canary H100: leak rate dropped to ~0.02GB/min, fragmentation reduced. But throughput 3% lower under synthetic decode microbench.

irene: that's promising. we should also add a smoke test that runs cross-GPU long-context workload and asserts resident decreases after eviction window. Add to canary pipeline.

anya: agreed. I'll open a PR with the epoch-CAS change + a stress test and bench results. tagging @ryan for review.

ryan: lgtm to iterate. let's also add a short-term mitigator: when we detect eviction misses > threshold, trigger synchronous drain on streams that touched the model (expensive but avoids runaway). Keep that behind a flag.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary runtime build kv-pt-epoch-cas -> h100-canary at 2025-11-09T16:00:00Z :construction_worker:

anya: deploying now to h100-canary. i'll drop updates in this thread after a few hours. :thumbsup:

felix: one more note — profiling showed lots of small cudaMemcpyAsync rebinds in the hot path. batching those rebinds or deferring rebind-to-epoch boundary further reduces the race window. might be worth exploring more aggressive batching as an Optimize knob.

anya: good call. follow-up: add metrics for "eviction_miss_count" and "slot_epoch_mismatch" to console so we can alert.

ryan: perfect. thanks all.

anya: update (2h): canary run reduced resident growth to noise. will roll to prod-canary tomorrow after rollout window.
